He lived between 7th and 8th century CE and is considered as one of the greatest scholars of Jainism. He wrote several religious texts, including the 'Haribhadra-bindu-shastra'. This work is an important source of Jain logic and epistemology.

Dharmakanta was the name of a powerful king who ruled the Vatsa kingdom around 4th century BCE. He is mentioned in several Buddhist texts, particularly the 'Ashokavadana', where he is described as a great patron of Buddhism. He is said to have built several stupas and funded the construction of the Bodhi tree in Bodhgaya.
